cleanIntro: The ZEROED 556, 30, 36 and 46 are SEALED rifle-caliber suppressors: CMMG says the front cap and inner baffles are laser welded into a single unit, and its book prints no procedure that opens the body, so nothing in this guide does. What CMMG does publish is real maintenance on the outside of that sealed tube: the can off the host's threaded muzzle, the HUB direct thread mount unscrewed from the body so the mount, the threads and the blast chamber can be cleaned and oiled, a bore brush with solvent but NEVER a patch, a heavier solvent clean with the can still closed, and a flush routine for a can that has been in water. CMMG's interval is before and after every use. The four cans differ in caliber (5.56, .30, 9mm/.36 and .46), and the ZEROED 46 takes a 1/2 drive in its front cap where the others take 3/8. CMMG also sets a minimum barrel length for each can and caliber; check its table before the can goes on a short barrel.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded and the ACTION OPEN before the can comes off
steps.action: Make the host firearm safe first: unloaded, with the action OPEN so you can see it is clear. CMMG asks for the action open specifically, every time the ZEROED goes on or comes off.
steps.prose: Everything in this guide happens with a hand at the muzzle end. That is why the action stays open.
steps.quote: Make sure firearm is unloaded and the action is open to verify clear before removing your suppressor from the host firearm.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.6

steps.title: ⛔ Let it COOL, or wear gloves
steps.action: Let the suppressor cool to the temperature of the room before you take it off or work on it. If it has to come off hot, wear protective gloves.
steps.prose: A can after a string of fire is hot enough to burn badly, and it does not look hot.
steps.quote: Allow suppressor to cool to ambient temperature before removal and/or service. If suppressor must be removed or installed while hot, protective gloves should be worn.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Safety notices, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Know what goes through it: NO unjacketed lead
steps.action: Never shoot ammunition with unjacketed lead bullets through a ZEROED. CMMG's reason is that the lead it leaves inside cannot be removed, and on a sealed can there is no way in to try. The cans are full-auto rated, at about 240 rounds between cooldown periods.
steps.prose: This is the one rule that decides whether a sealed can can ever be cleaned at all.
steps.aside: ZEROED 556, 30, 36, and 46 suppressors have a full-auto rated rating. Approximately 240 rounds between cooldown periods.
steps.quote: Do NOT use ammunition with unjacketed lead projectiles in any sealed ZEROED suppressor. Unjacketed projectiles will leave lead deposits that CANNOT be removed.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Ammunition, printed p.8

steps.title: Off the host: grasp the body, counter-clockwise
steps.action: With the suppressor and the firearm cool to the touch, grip the suppressor body firmly and turn it counter-clockwise to unthread it from the muzzle. If the direct thread mount is stuck, put a 7/8" wrench on the flats at the rear of the suppressor for more leverage.
steps.prose: Turn the body, not the barrel. The wrench goes on the mount's flats, never on the tube.
steps.aside: If direct thread mount is stuck, use a 7/8” wrench on the flats at the rear of the suppressor for more leverage.
steps.quote: With the suppressor and firearm cool to the touch, firmly grasp the suppressor body and turn counter-clockwise to un-thread.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.6

steps.title: HUB mount off the body: 7/8" wrench, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Hold the suppressor body firmly in one hand, or put a 3/8 drive ratchet or breaker bar into the front cap for leverage (1/2 drive on the ZEROED 46). Then put a 7/8" wrench on the direct thread mount and unthread it counter-clockwise. CMMG's regular maintenance includes cleaning the mount surfaces, the threads and the blast chamber, and those are only reachable with the mount off.
steps.prose: The mount went on at 30 ft-lb, so expect it to be tight.
steps.aside: Firmly grasp the suppressor body in one hand or insert a 3/8 drive ratchet (1/2 for ZEROED 46) or breaker bar into the front cap for additional leverage.
steps.quote: Use a 7/8” wrench on the direct thread mount to unthread counter-clockwise.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — HUB Mount Removal, printed p.7

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes: the body is SEALED
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. CMMG states that the ZEROED 556, 30, 36 and 46 are a sealed design with the front cap and inner baffles laser welded into one unit, and its book prints no procedure for opening the body. With the can off the host and the mount off the body, everything below is cleaning on a closed tube.
steps.prose: A sealed can is not a can you have failed to open. If something inside is wrong, it goes back to CMMG.
steps.quote: ZEROED 556, 30, 36, and 46 are a sealed suppressor design, eliminating much of the disassembly required for general cleaning and maintenance such as the front cap and inner baffles which are laser welded into a single unit.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Inspect it: bore, a shake, the outside
steps.action: Look through the bore for any obstruction or foreign object. Shake the can and listen for anything broken or loose inside. On a sealed can that is the only internal check you have. Then check the outside for dents or other damage. CMMG wants this before and after every use.
steps.prose: A rattle, a blocked bore or a dented tube means the can does not go back on the host until CMMG has seen it.
steps.aside: Visually inspect the bore of the suppressor for any obstructions or foreign objects.
steps.quote: Shake the suppressor and listen to check for any broken or detached internal parts.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Mount, threads and blast chamber: clean and lightly oil
steps.action: With the mount off, clean the HUB mount's surfaces and threads, the suppressor body's threads and the blast chamber, then put a light coat of oil on them.
steps.prose: Light oil means light. Anti-seize goes on the threads when the mount goes back in.
steps.quote: Remove, clean, and lightly oil the HUB mount surfaces and threads as well as the suppressor body threads and blast chamber.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.7

steps.title: Bore: brush and solvent, NEVER a patch
steps.action: For lighter cleaning, use a bore brush and gun cleaning solvent to take carbon buildup and fouling out of the suppressor bore. Do not run a cleaning patch through it: a patch can lodge inside the sealed can and cause damage the next time the host is fired.
steps.prose: The brush comes back out on the rod. A patch has nothing holding it.
steps.quote: For lighter cleaning, a bore brush and gun cleaning solvent may be used to remove any carbon buildup or fouling from the bore of the suppressor.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.7
steps.warn: Do NOT run cleaning patches through the bore of the suppressor as they could become lodged inside the suppressor and cause damage upon firing.

steps.title: Heavier cleaning: kit or soak, then stand it HUB-threads DOWN to drain
steps.action: CMMG calls this deep cleaning, but the can stays closed: a suppressor-safe cleaning kit, or an ultrasonic cleaner only with a solvent approved for ultrasonic use and safe for the material. Take the mount off the body first. Afterwards stand the can on a clean towel with the HUB threaded end down and the front cap up, so standing solvent runs down the baffle stack and out through the bore hole. Let it dry completely before anything is oiled, the threads get anti-seize, or it goes back together.
steps.prose: Solvent left inside a sealed can has nowhere to go but out the muzzle the next time you fire it. Give it the time to drain and dry.
steps.caution: If using an ultrasonic cleaner, make sure solvent is approved for ultrasonic use and material safe.
steps.aside: Allow the suppressor to completely dry before lightly oiling surfaces, applying anti-seize to threads, and re-assembling.
steps.quote: If deep cleaned, remove the mount from the body and stand the suppressor up on a clean towel with the HUB threaded side facing down and front cap facing up to allow any standing solvent to run down the baffle stack and drain through the bore hole.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.7

steps.title: If it has been in water: drain, flush hot, dry, oil
steps.action: Do this as soon as you can after the can has been used in or exposed to water. Let it drain completely. Soak and flush it with very hot water and detergent, draining between rounds, three to four times at least. Then soak and flush it with clean boiling water. Dry it with compressed air through the can if you have it, or overnight in an oven on its warm or lowest setting if time allows. Once it is thoroughly dry, lubricate the mount and threads.
steps.prose: Do not shoot it wet unless you truly have to. CMMG's word is absolutely necessary.
steps.aside: After the suppressor has been thoroughly dried, lubricate the mount and threads.
steps.quote: Soak and flush the suppressor with very hot water and a detergent. Drain and repeat this procedure a minimum of 3-4 times.
steps.cite: CMMG ZEROED 556 | 30 | 36 | 46 — SUPPRESSOR USER MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Maintenance after water exposure, printed p.8
steps.warn: Allow to drain completely and DO NOT use the suppressor unless absolutely necessary.

deepAbsentReason: CMMG's book calls the ZEROED 556, 30, 36 and 46 a sealed suppressor design, with the front cap and inner baffles laser welded into a single unit (printed p.6), and prints no procedure that opens the body. The deepest work it publishes is taking the HUB mount off the body (printed p.7), a heavier clean with a suppressor-safe kit or approved solvent with the can still closed (printed p.7), and the flush after water exposure (printed p.8). CMMG makes those part of its regular maintenance, and they are in the routine lane above. A can believed defective goes back to CMMG: the book asks the owner to contact CMMG Customer Service to arrange a return, with a return authorization issued before anything ships, and not to return it to the retailer (printed p.10). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: INSPECTION — BEFORE AND AFTER USE
tasks: Look through the bore for obstructions or foreign objects.
Shake the can and listen for anything broken or detached inside.
Check the outside for dents or other damage.

cleaning.name: MOUNT, THREADS & BLAST CHAMBER
tasks: HUB mount off the body: 7/8" wrench, counter-clockwise.
Clean the mount surfaces and threads, the body threads and the blast chamber.
A light coat of oil on those surfaces.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore brush and gun cleaning solvent for carbon and fouling.
⛔ Never run a cleaning patch through the bore.

cleaning.name: HEAVIER CLEAN & DRY
tasks: Mount off the body; a suppressor-safe cleaning kit, the can stays closed.
Ultrasonic only with a solvent approved for ultrasonic use and material safe.
Stand it on a clean towel, HUB threads down, front cap up, to drain.
Completely dry before oiling, anti-seize or reassembly.

cleaning.name: AFTER WATER EXPOSURE
tasks: As soon as possible: drain completely.
Very hot water and detergent, soak and flush, at least 3–4 times.
A soak and flush with clean boiling water.
Dry with compressed air, or overnight in an oven on warm.
Once thoroughly dry: lubricate the mount and threads.

reassembly: Mounting surfaces and threads clean; a light coat of oil on the mount surfaces and a thin coat of anti-seize on the threads, to prevent galling or seizing.
Thread the direct thread mount into the suppressor body clockwise, taking care not to cross-thread it.
Once hand tight, tighten the mount to 30 ft-lb with a 7/8" wrench or socket.
Host firearm unloaded, with the action open to verify clear.
Muzzle devices, thread protectors and crush washers off the host; muzzle threads inspected and cleaned if needed.
Thread the can onto the muzzle clockwise without cross-threading, until it is firmly hand tight and square to the muzzle with no gaps.
CMMG recommends checking bore alignment with a caliber-appropriate alignment rod.
fncheck: With the host firearm unloaded and the action open: the can is firmly hand tight and sits square on the muzzle with no gap, and if the mount was off the body it went back in at 30 ft-lb. Look through the bore for obstructions, shake the can and listen for anything loose inside, and, as CMMG recommends, check bore alignment with a caliber-appropriate alignment rod.
